title: Age estimation in crustaceans: established methods (growth bands and lipofuscin) and emerging molecular approaches (DNA methylation)
content:
Abstract
Crustaceans contain calcified structures like the gastric mill and eyestalks that exhibit distinct banding patterns (growth bands). These bands can be counted to estimate chronological age. Crustacean age has been traditionally estimated indirectly through length-frequency analysis, which provides relative rather than chronological age. Tagging can yield reliable results but is time-consuming and costly. Growth band and lipofuscin analyses offer more direct and accurate age estimations, making them preferable for precise assessments. We review the literature on these two techniques while also exploring a recent promising approach using DNA methylation. Growth bands in the gastric mill and lipofuscin accumulation in the brain have been successfully applied to aging crustaceans. Both indicators show a linear relationship with growth, and validation using captive-reared individuals have further confirmed the reliability of these techniques. DNA methylation has been developed in other aquatic organisms, but studies on crustaceans have been limited.
